modern: Does the sun take on the work of the rain, or Aesculapius the work of the Fruit-bearer, the earth? And how is it with each of the stars—are they not different, and yet they work together to the same end?
original: Does the sun undertake to do the work of the rain, or Aesculapius the work of the Fruit-bearer [the earth]? And how is it with respect to each of the stars—are they not different and yet they work together to the same end?
notification: Does the sun take on the work of the rain, or Aesculapius the work of the Fruit-bearer, the earth?
notification_original: Does the sun undertake to do the work of the rain, or Aesculapius the work of the Fruit-bearer [the earth]?

explained.summary: Everything in nature has its own job. The sun doesn’t try to be rain, and the stars all differ, yet together they make one working whole. People are the same: you don’t have to do everyone’s part, only your own, and do it well, trusting that different roles add up to something shared.
